g.id: Quantities: pipe length by diameter, reservoir volume
Unit rates: OMR per metre, OMR per cubic metre
Add 10 percent preliminaries and 20 percent contingency
STEP 1. CAPEX: what it costs to build, one number, today's rials
0.5 percent of pipe and reservoir cost, 3 percent for chlorination
STEP 2. OPEX: what it costs to run, every year
1,000 OMR per month per pumping station
Water sold: volume times the published NWS tariff, 0.660 domestic and 1.210 non-domestic OMR per cubic metre
STEP 3. Income: what comes in, every year
Connection charge: paid once when a customer joins, not every year
Free tanker contracts NWS no longer has to pay
STEP 4. Payback in months = CAPEX minus the one-off connection charges, divided by yearly income minus yearly OPEX
STEP 6. Compare CAPEX, OPEX and payback, with a written list of pros and cons
THE GAPS: a rial in year 25 is counted as a rial today, so there is no NPV. Cost is the only thing scored. No assumption is ever tested.
